name: React.memo()
description: A higher-order component that skips re-rendering a component if its props are shallowly equal to the previous render's props.
parameters: Component — the component to memoize. arePropsEqual — optional custom comparison function.
notes: Only helps when the component re-renders often with the same props and rendering it is non-trivial; wrap function props passed to it with useCallback so they don't defeat the memoization.

name: forwardRef()
description: Lets a component receive a ref from its parent and forward it to one of its own children, typically an underlying DOM node.
returns: A component that accepts a ref prop.
notes: Needed because refs aren't passed through props automatically like other values.

name: lazy()
description: Defines a component that is loaded via dynamic import only when it's first rendered, enabling code-splitting.
parameters: loader — a function returning a Promise that resolves to a module with a default export component.
returns: A component that must be rendered inside a Suspense boundary.
notes: Reduces the initial bundle size by splitting rarely-needed screens/components into separate chunks loaded on demand.

name: Suspense
description: A component that shows a fallback UI while its descendants are still 'loading' — such as a lazy-loaded component or data fetched via Suspense-compatible libraries.
parameters: fallback — the UI to show while children aren't ready.
notes: Works with React.lazy() out of the box; using it directly for data fetching requires a framework or library that supports Suspense-based fetching.

name: createPortal()
description: Renders children into a different part of the DOM tree than the component's normal parent hierarchy, while keeping them part of the same React tree for events and context.
parameters: children — the React content to render. domNode — the target DOM node to render into.
notes: Commonly used for modals, tooltips, and dropdowns that need to escape a parent's overflow:hidden or z-index stacking context.

name: StrictMode
description: A development-only wrapper that helps surface potential problems by intentionally double-invoking certain functions (component bodies, some hooks) and warning about deprecated APIs.
notes: Has no effect on the production build — it's purely a development aid for catching side effects in render and other unsafe patterns.

name: cloneElement()
description: Creates a copy of a React element with new or merged props, used to inject additional props into children passed to a component.
parameters: element — the element to clone. newProps — props to merge onto the clone.
notes: Considered a legacy pattern in most cases — render props, composition, or context are usually clearer alternatives.

name: Children Utilities
description: A set of utility functions (map, forEach, count, only, toArray) for safely working with the opaque `props.children` structure, which can be a single node, an array, or nested arrays.
returns: Depends on the method — e.g. React.Children.count() returns a number, React.Children.toArray() returns a flat array.
notes: Rarely needed if children are treated simply as opaque renderable content — mostly useful when a component must inspect or transform its children individually.

name: act()
description: A testing utility (from `react` / `react-dom/test-utils`) that ensures all state updates, effects, and re-renders triggered inside the callback are flushed before assertions run.
parameters: callback — function (sync or async) containing the code that triggers React updates.
returns: A Promise if the callback is async, otherwise undefined.
notes: Testing Library's render/fireEvent already wrap calls in act() internally, so it's rarely needed to call directly in tests using that library.

name: createRoot()
description: The React DOM API (from `react-dom/client`) used to create a root and render a React element tree into a DOM container, enabling concurrent features.
parameters: container — the DOM element to render into.
returns: A root object with render() and unmount() methods.
notes: Replaced the legacy ReactDOM.render() API starting in React 18; ReactDOM.render() no longer enables concurrent features.
